name: Aguachile Verde — Sinaloa-Style Shrimp in Green Chile-Lime
subtitle: Sinaloa-Style Shrimp in Green Chile-Lime
description: Butterflied raw shrimp "cooked" briefly in a blended lime, serrano and cilantro water, piled with cucumber and red onion and eaten right away on tostadas. Serves 4 as a starter.

ingredients.text: 450 g large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
ingredients.item: large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

ingredients.text: 1 cucumber, peeled, seeded and sliced into half-moons
ingredients.item: cucumber, peeled, seeded and sliced into half-moons

steps.text: Butterfly 450 g large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined: cut almost all the way through along the back and open them flat. Put them on a chilled platter in a single layer and sprinkle with 1 tsp salt.
Blend 180 ml fresh lime juice (about 8 limes), 3 serrano chiles, stemmed, 20 g cilantro, with stems, 1 small garlic clove and 60 ml cold water for 30 seconds, until bright green and smooth.

Pour the chile-lime water over the shrimp and scatter 1/2 red onion, very thinly sliced and 1 cucumber, peeled, seeded and sliced into half-moons on top. Refrigerate 15 minutes, until the shrimp turn just pink-opaque at the edges but stay translucent in the center.
Top with 1 avocado, sliced and serve immediately with 8 tostadas or saltine crackers.

notes: Unlike ceviche, aguachile isn't left to marinate: in Sinaloa it's served within minutes, so the shrimp stays tender and sweet. Use the freshest shrimp you can find (frozen-at-sea shrimp, thawed in the fridge, are often fresher than "fresh"). A dash of Maggi or Clamato in the blender is a popular local touch.
